HorizonTrust is evaluating Dedicated/private deployment for regulatory reasons and wants clear SLA and incident playbook details plus KMS/SAML integration notes.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll kick off, we have Luis from SE and Anika from CSM. 
[00:08] Karen Li: Thanks, Maya. Karen Li, CISO at HorizonTrust. We've got Tom and Priya with me. We're specifically here to go over incident response, BCDR, SLA, and escalation.
[00:16] Luis Ortega: Hi all, Luis - I'll go over the technical bits, DR, encryption, KMS integration, and how we manage RTO/RPO with Dedicated or Private deployments.
[00:24] Tom Reynolds: Quick ask up front - we need to ensure data residency and auditable logs for regulators, plus HSM-backed key management.
[00:30] Maya Thompson: Absolutely, that's in scope. Quick agenda: attestations, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS, then incident response and SLA. Sound good?
[00:38] Ethan Moore: Yep. Also we want to see how your escalation works during a partial outage - steps, comms, playbooks.
[00:44] Maya Thompson: Great. I'll hand to Luis for the tech overview.
[00:46] Luis Ortega: Ok, so on encryption - at rest we use AES-256 and by default we manage keys, but for enterprise we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM - commonly Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS. We do envelope encryption and you can bring your own key, rotate keys, and we support HSM-backed keys for the private deployments.
[01:04] Priya Sharma: When you say "support" KMS, is the ciphertext stored in Redwood or in customer storage? What's the responsibility boundary?
[01:11] Luis Ortega: Good question. Ciphertext always stored in Redwood's object storage for hosted/Dedicated. Keys are never stored in plaintext here - we call customer KMS for decryption at runtime, or if you're on private deployment, the calls stay inside your VPC. There's a short-lived key cache to reduce latency but keys are not persisted in plaintext.
[01:28] Karen Li: We need to see a diagram of that flow and an assurance about audit logs for key access.
[01:34] Luis Ortega: We'll send a KMS integration diagram, including audit hooks - CloudTrail style logs for AWS KMS, and logs for Azure Key Vault calls.
[01:40] Maya Thompson: We'll include notes about separation of duties and RBAC - we integrate with SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for users and roles. We also support fine-grained RBAC in the Console for route-level permissions.
[01:50] Tom Reynolds: SCIM provisioning - can you sync groups from our Azure AD and map to roles?
[01:54] Luis Ortega: Yes, group mapping works. It's near real-time provisioning; we'll share the SCIM spec and attributes. Some edge cases in older AD setups require custom mapping but we can do that in the onboarding project.
[02:06] Ethan Moore: Audit logs retention - what length do you keep logs, and can we get them exported to our SIEM?
[02:11] Maya Thompson: By default audit logs are retained 90 days in the Console. For enterprise we have log export connectors - you can stream audit logs to your S3/Event Hub/Log Analytics workspace. We also offer extended retention as an add-on.
[02:22] Priya Sharma: Important for us is immutable logs for regulatory audit. Is integrity guaranteed?
[02:26] Luis Ortega: We support append-only storage with tamper-evident markers; for strict immutability in some deployments we can provide WORM settings or ship logs to your storage.
[02:34] Maya Thompson: Ok shifting to incident response & BCDR. Luis, can you outline our tiered incident model?
[02:39] Luis Ortega: Sure. We use Sev 1-3 definitions. Sev-1 is total system outage impacting >90% requests for a route; Sev-2 is partial outage or significant degradation; Sev-3 is minor impact. RTO/RPO targets depend on deployment: for hosted the SLA for critical routes is 99.9% by default, we offer 99.95/99.99 for Dedicated with contractual SLAs. RTO for Sev-1 - our goal is failover or mitigation within 15-30 minutes for critical endpoints; RPO goal is near-zero for KV cacheable requests but depends on data type.
[03:10] Karen Li: Your 'near-zero' phrasing doesn't fly in audit. We need concrete RTO/RPO numbers and the mechanisms - how do you failover, what are the recovery steps, who is on call?
[03:19] Luis Ortega: Understood. For Dedicated we run cross-zone replicas for state; failover is automated with health checks and we have documented runbooks that the on-call uses. We'll provide explicit RTOs: 15 minutes for automated failover for network issues, 30 minutes for degraded node replacement, RPO under 1 minute for config and predicted KV cache states - though for long-running context-heavy sessions there are limitations, we document the caveats.
[03:39] Tom Reynolds: So for regulatory needs we likely need guaranteed RTO 30m and RPO under 5 minutes. Can you commit contractually?
[03:46] Maya Thompson: That's exactly what Dedicated is for - SLA-backed uptime and latency. We can include RTO/RPO commitments in the contract for Dedicated and Private with specific remedies. We'll loop legal to work those terms with your procurement.
[03:56] Priya Sharma: Escalation - how do we get notified? Email? Pager? Slack? We need an on-call rotation and a clear path to exec escalation.
[04:03] Luis Ortega: Notification channels: we use PagerDuty for Sev-1 and Sev-2 P1s, email + webhooks for other alerts. For enterprise accounts we set up a dedicated escalation path: first-level on-call (SRE) -> Engineering lead -> Account owner -> Customer success/Eng VP. For exec escalation, we have an A-team contact list.
[04:18] Ethan Moore: Is there a 24/7 follow-the-sun on-call for Dedicated customers?
[04:22] Maya Thompson: Yes, Dedicated customers get 24/7 support and a prioritized escalation queue.
[04:26] Karen Li: We also need BCDR proof - have you run tabletop exercises and do you share postmortems?
[04:32] Luis Ortega: We run quarterly DR tests internally; for enterprise customers we offer joint tabletop exercises. Post-incident we publish a redacted postmortem with timeline, root cause, mitigations and we can provide a sanitized version for audits.
[04:44] Priya Sharma: For a Sev-1 outage, what is the customer communication cadence?
[04:48] Anika Patel: We do immediate acknowledgement within 15 minutes for Sev-1 with initial triage update; follow-ups at 30m, 1h, and then hourly until resolution, and a detailed post-incident report within 72 hours. We'll include actions and timelines.
[04:59] Tom Reynolds: That's close to what we expect. What about maintenance windows and scheduled upgrades - how do you notify and is there a maintenance SLA?
[05:07] Luis Ortega: We give at least 48 hours notice for planned maint; maintenance windows are configurable for Dedicated and Private. For hosted there are low-impact rolling upgrades - we target zero-downtime but provide maintenance SLAs for Dedicated if uptime is affected.
[05:19] Karen Li: Let's talk about audit access. During an audit we need logs, control evidence, and possibly access to a test environment. How does that work?
[05:26] Maya Thompson: We provide SOC 2 Type II reports under NDA. For deeper audits we can provide read-only access to a compliance bundle and sample logs. For Private deployments we can give broader access since you control the environment.
[05:36] Priya Sharma: Encryption key rotation - how often and can we force rotations?
[05:40] Luis Ortega: You control rotation schedules for customer-managed keys; we recommend 90-day rotation but support more frequent. For platform-managed keys we rotate keys regularly and will notify customers. Key-rotation is orchestrated to avoid service disruption; we'll share a rotation playbook.
[05:53] Ethan Moore: What about data residency - can you restrict inference processing to specific regions?
[05:57] Maya Thompson: Yes, you can pin workloads to region or deploy Private. Hosted supports region routing and Dedicated can be provisioned in your desired cloud region or private data center for residency.
[06:06] Tom Reynolds: Can you run a quick scenario - say an upstream cloud provider outage in us-east-1 takes down a subset of instances. Walk through the steps.
[06:12] Luis Ortega: Sure. Step 1: Detection via health checks and telemetry, triggers an automatic route failover to replicas in us-west-2. Step 2: On-call gets paged, incident declared if traffic drop > threshold. Step 3: Traffic is routed and cache warming strategies applied to maintain latency; if cross-region failover cannot meet latency SLOs we apply degraded-mode with reduced context retention and notify customer. Step 4: Once provider is back, we do traffic reweighting and state resync. Post-incident we run RCA and provide mitigation actions.
[06:43] Karen Li: That resync step worries me - is there a chance of data loss?
[06:47] Luis Ortega: Data loss risk is low due to cross-zone replication and write-ahead logs for critical state; our documented RPO is sub-1 minute for critical metadata. We will include the exact mechanisms in the architecture doc.
[06:58] Priya Sharma: For session / prompt data that isn't persisted, how do you guarantee customer privacy during DR operations?
[07:03] Maya Thompson: We treat ephemeral prompts as transient; for compliance sensitive customers we recommend Dedicated/Private and explicit configuration to avoid long retention. Also encryption in transit and at rest applies.
[07:13] Tom Reynolds: On the SLA side, what are the credits/remedies if you miss uptime targets?
[07:17] Maya Thompson: Standard SLA credits are tiered: if uptime < target we offer service credits scaled to downtime percentage. For contractual Dedicated agreements we can negotiate termination or higher remedies but that requires legal review.
[07:28] Ethan Moore: We will need those credit schedules in writing.
[07:31] Maya Thompson: We'll include the SLA pdf in the pack.
[07:34] Karen Li: Regarding escalation contacts - we want named roles and phone/pager for Sev-1 after hours.
[07:39] Anika Patel: We'll provide a dedicated escalation contact list with on-call rotation; phone/pager for Sev-1 and a named account executive for business continuity.
[07:47] Priya Sharma: Can you provide an example runbook for a network partition?
[07:50] Luis Ortega: Yes, we have a network partition runbook - detection, reroute, cache strategy, mitigation, and postmortem checklist. We'll attach an anonymized exemplar.
[07:58] Tom Reynolds: Good. For audits we may ask for evidence of tabletop exercises and runbook updates - do you have logs of those?
[08:04] Maya Thompson: Yes, we can provide schedules and artifacts for joint exercises.
[08:08] Ethan Moore: What about change control - how do you track code/infra changes that could affect availability?
[08:12] Luis Ortega: We have a change management process with staged rollouts, feature flags, and canary analysis. All changes are logged; for Dedicated we can coordinate maintenance windows if you need freeze periods before audits.
[08:24] Karen Li: On reporting post-incident - you said 72 hours for a detailed report. Is that always possible?
[08:29] Anika Patel: For Sev-1 we commit to an initial triage within 72 hours and a full postmortem within 7 days in most cases; we'll set expectations in the contract.
[08:38] Priya Sharma: For legal/regulatory requests we may need a timeline of data access requests and logs - can you provide those?
[08:44] Maya Thompson: Yes, we keep an audit trail for data access, and can provide.redacted timelines for legal requests. For Private deployments, you control access.
[08:53] Tom Reynolds: Let's confirm some concrete numbers to include in the docs you send: Desired RTO 30 minutes for Sev-1, RPO under 5 minutes, and 99.95% target SLA. Can Redwood meet those for Dedicated?
[09:05] Luis Ortega: Yes, for Dedicated we can commit to 99.95% and RTO 30 minutes, RPO under 5 minutes in contract; we'll work with legal on the specifics.
[09:14] Karen Li: Excellent. Also include a timeline for onboarding and a pilot where we test DR scenarios.
[09:19] Maya Thompson: We'll propose a 6-week pilot with a DR tabletop in week 4.
[09:24] Ethan Moore: Make sure the pilot includes synthetic traffic and a cross-region failover run.
[09:28] Luis Ortega: Noted. We'll outline scope.
[09:31] Priya Sharma: A couple of nitty-gritty items - do you provide signed BAA or specific certifications for payments data?
[09:36] Maya Thompson: We can provide a BAA for HIPAA-covered workloads; we also have PCI considerations - we'll confirm the attestation scope in the package.
[09:44] Tom Reynolds: Ok, any blockers from our side? We need to check internal legal and procurement timelines - expecting 60-90 days for contract review.
[09:52] Karen Li: Also we need a presales checklist of what you need to provision Dedicated: network peering, IP ranges, VPN, and KMS tenancy.
[09:59] Anika Patel: We'll send a provisioning checklist with network requirements and onboarding steps.
[10:04] Maya Thompson: Quick recap of agreed actions - send SOC 2/ISO, SLA pdf, KMS diagram, SCIM guide, runbook examples, and propose pilot schedule.
[10:12] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. Can we get the docs by end of week?
[10:15] Maya Thompson: Yes, we'll aim for 2026-09-17.
[10:18] Ethan Moore: Final question - how long do you keep backups and what is the retention policy for customer data if we terminate?
[10:24] Luis Ortega: We keep backups per policy; for Hosted default retention is 30 days, can be extended. On termination we will securely wipe customer data per contract and can provide certificate of deletion. We'll include retention matrix.
[10:36] Karen Li: Ok, thanks everyone. We'll review the assets and get back with our timelines.
[10:40] Maya Thompson: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the pack and schedule the tabletop.
[10:44] Anika Patel: I'll send calendar invites for the proposed dates.
[10:47] Tom Reynolds: Thanks.
[10:49] [Meeting ends]
